title: How to Test Ad Creatives on a Small Budget | AIVideosUGC
description: An ad creative is the video or photo in your ad. Test a few versions together from one photo, change one thing at a time, and read the results.
h1: How to Test Ad Creatives Without Guessing
lead: To test ad creatives (the video or photo in the ad), change one thing at a time. Make a few versions from the same photo or a product link, and run them together before you spend more. A version can include a script, which is the words to say. It can include an AI actor. It can include a voiceover, a spoken voice.
secondary_keywords: ad creative testing for small business
summary: Change one thing, run a few versions on the same audience and budget, and read the result only after each version has actually played.

sections.h2: What Is an AI Video Ad You Can Test?
paras: An AI video ad is a short clip you pay to show, made from your product. It can include opening words, a presenter, a spoken voice, and the edit that joins them. You can start from a photo, a short description, or the product page link.
The test rules do not change. Change one thing between files. Use the same audience and the same budget. Read the result only after each file has actually played.

sections.h2: How Do I Compare Ad Versions From One Product?
paras: Keep the photo, the length, and the shape (tall, square, or wide) the same. Change only how the clip starts.

For a plain round wall clock, one version can start as the face comes into focus at dawn. Another can start as a hand hangs it on kitchen tile. A third can start as the clock leaves its box. Photo ads work the same way. A mug can sit on a counter, on a desk, or as a wrapped gift. Use the same mug, and add the same words later. When the only change is the presenter or the tone, ask for that, and do not swap the product. Build the photo versions with the [AI ad image generator](page:social-ad-photos).

Home brand. Example: one photo becomes a clip, and the room stays the room in the photo.

sections.h2: How Do I Keep Ad Creative Testing Fair for a Small Business?
paras: Change only one thing between versions. If the opening, the setting, and the offer all move at once, you spend money and learn nothing.
Worth testing, one at a time: the opening moment, the setting, the shape, the length, and the words you add afterward. Start with the opening. It decides whether anyone sees the rest.

sections.h2: How Should the Versions Run Side by Side?
paras: Put them in one campaign, one group of ads, with the same audience, the same budget, and the same product page.

Many ad accounts let several ads share one group. Some also offer a built-in test that shows each version to part of the audience. The account may spend more on one version early. A version that barely ran has not been tested. Do not edit the ads while the test is live. A change can make the ad account start the test over, so the result is no longer clear.
sections.alt: Adult hands hold the same plain round wall clock in two matched side-by-side positions.

sections.h2: How Do I Tell Which Ad Version Works?
paras: Wait several days, and do not call a winner from one afternoon or from a version that hardly played.

Read three numbers in order. First, how many people stay past the opening. That tells you if the start works. Second, the click rate, how often people click. That tells you if they wanted to visit. Third, the cost per purchase, or per add-to-cart, each time someone adds the item to the cart. That matters most for the shop. A version can get more views and still lose on sales. If the numbers are close, that change did not matter much. Keep the one you prefer and test a bigger difference next.
sections.alt: Hands rest beside blank color cards and the same plain round wall clock.

sections.h2: What Should the Next Test Change?
paras: Turn off the clear losers. Keep the version that brings sales at a cost you can accept, and change one new thing.

Write down the date, what changed, and the result. After a few rounds you will see what your buyers respond to. When a winner starts costing more per sale, make fresh versions. Work through the opening, the setting, the shape, the length, then the offer. Each round starts from what already worked.

faq.q: How many versions should a small shop run?
faq.a: Start with a few, often three. More than that splits a small budget so far that no version gets a fair chance to run. Every extra version is another file you make.
Test the opening. It decides whether anyone watches the rest. Keep the product, the length, and the shape (tall, square, or wide) the same until that result is clear.

faq.q: Can I change the price on only one version?
faq.a: Not while you are testing the video or the photo. Put the same words, the same price, and the same music on every file. Test the offer in a later round, on its own.

faq.q: Where do the numbers come from?
faq.a: From your ad account, where real viewers produce the result. The versions are made here. The comparison happens there.

faq.q: What if the ad account barely shows one version?
faq.a: Do not treat it as a loser. Use the test tool inside your ad account, or put each version in its own group, so each version actually runs.

faq.q: How many credits does a test round use?
faq.a: Each clip is its own file: 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Credits are what you spend. You see the cost before you start. If a file does not finish, the credits come back.

faq.q: What is inside a generated version?
faq.a: A script (the words), a generated presenter, a spoken voice, and the edit, made from a photo, a short description, or a product link. Captions, timed words on the video, can be in the file when you ask for them.

faq.a: Yes. Download a tall (9:16), square (1:1), or wide (16:9) file and post it on TikTok, Meta (Facebook and Instagram), or YouTube. You can also make 4:3 and 3:4.
